title: Columns
novel:
Ted's boss gave him his first [[solo|solo]] [[project|project]]: design a [[skyscraper|skyscraper]] [[lobby|lobby]] for a major [[client|client]]. But there was one problem — the client, a [[stubborn|stubborn]] [[billionaire|billionaire]] named Mr. [[Bilson|Bilson]], [[insisted|insist]] on adding a [[huge|huge]] [[column|column]] in the middle of the room. A column that would [[ruin|ruin]] the entire [[design|design]].

"It's [[structural|structure]]," Bilson said. "You can't have a building without columns."

"Actually you can," Ted argued. "With modern [[cantilevers|cantilever]] and [[reinforced|reinforce]] [[concrete|concrete]] —"

"I want the column. It's [[tradition|tradition]]."

Ted spent weeks trying to convince him. He made [[elaborate|elaborate]] [[presentations|presentation]], built [[scale models|scale model]], and even wrote a [[poem|poem]] about the [[beauty|beautiful]] of open spaces. Bilson was not moved.

"The column stays," he said. "Or you're fired."

Meanwhile, Marshall and Lily were dealing with their own conflicts. Lily wanted to [[redecorate|redecorate]] the apartment; Marshall loved it exactly the way it was, right down to the [[mysterious|mysterious]] [[stain|stain]] on the [[ceiling|ceiling]]. "That stain has been there since college!" Marshall protested. "Exactly!" Lily said.

In the end, Ted found a [[compromise|compromise]]. He designed a column that was not just structural but [[artistic|artistic]] — a [[sculpture|sculpture]] that told the story of the building's construction, from the first [[brick|brick]] to the final [[beam|beam]]. Bilson loved it. "You're a [[genius|genius]]," he said. "I know," Ted replied.

solo.en: done alone, without other people's help

project.en: a planned piece of work that takes time to complete

skyscraper.en: a very tall building in a city

lobby.en: the large entrance area of a hotel, office building, etc.

client.en: a person or company that pays for a service

stubborn.en: unwilling to change your mind, even when you are wrong

billionaire.en: a person who has more than a billion dollars

huge.en: extremely large in size or amount

column.en: a tall solid upright post that supports a building

structural.en: relating to the way something is built or organized

concrete.en: a hard building material made from cement, sand and stones

tradition.en: a belief or way of doing things that has existed for a long time

elaborate.en: containing a lot of careful detail

presentation.en: a talk or show that explains something to a group

scale model.en: a small copy of something made at an exact ratio

poem.en: a piece of writing in short lines expressing feelings or ideas

beauty.en: the quality of being pleasing to look at or experience

redecorate.en: to paint and decorate a room again in a new style

stain.en: a dirty mark on something that is hard to remove

ceiling.en: the upper surface of a room

compromise.en: an agreement reached by each side giving up something

artistic.en: relating to art or showing creative skill

sculpture.en: a piece of art made from stone, metal, wood, etc.

brick.en: a hard rectangular block used for building walls

beam.en: a long thick piece of steel or wood that supports a building
